req.title: DELETE rejects unknown player
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on DELETE for a non-existent playerId.

doc.reasoning: The DELETE endpoint is at /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}. R-PLAYER-015 requires HTTP 404 when the squad_number does not exist. Tests cover: (1) positive — a squad_number that exists returns 204 (verifying the happy path and that the route works at all); (2) negative — a squad_number that has never existed returns exactly 404; (3) boundary — squad_number 0 (below the minimum seeded value of 1) returns 404; (4) boundary+1 — squad_number 27 (one above the maximum seeded value of 26) returns 404; (5) state-transition — deleting an existing player then deleting again returns 404 on the second call, confirming the 404 path is triggered by absence not by some other condition. Test[4] (the double-delete test) was previously marked kind=negative with heuristic=STC. The violation rule requires that a negative kind test must not use heuristic=STC. Fix: change heuristic from STC to NEG, which is correct because the second DELETE exercises the error partition (non-existent resource) and NEG is the appropriate heuristic for error-pathway coverage. The state-transition reasoning is preserved in the trace. All assertions use exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations.

EP: squad_number in the seeded set → valid partition

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/10')
assert response.status_code == 204
assert response.content == b''

tests.name: test_delete_nonexistent_player_returns_404
expected: Response status code is exactly 404, not 200, 204, or 400
trace: R-PLAYER-015 — core requirement: DELETE of non-existent playerId must yield 404
NEG: squad_number outside seeded set → error partition
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/9999')
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.status_code != 204
assert response.status_code != 200

BVA: tests the lower boundary of the valid squad_number domain

tests.name: test_delete_squad_number_above_max_returns_404
preconditions: Database maximum squad_number is 26; squad_number 27 does not exist
expected: Response status code is exactly 404, not 204
trace: R-PLAYER-015 — boundary value one above the maximum seeded squad_number (26+1=27)
BVA: tests the upper boundary of the seeded domain; catches off-by-one mutations on the lookup
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/27')
assert response.status_code == 404
assert response.status_code != 204

tests.name: test_delete_twice_second_call_returns_404
actions: Send DELETE /players/squadnumber/5 (second call — player no longer exists)
expected: Status codes are exactly 204 then 404 — not swapped
trace: R-PLAYER-015 — state transition: exists→deleted→not-found; second DELETE must yield 404
NEG: second call exercises the error partition (absent resource); covers the transition from 'player present' state to 'player absent' state and verifies 404 on re-delete
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)
first = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/5')
assert first.status_code == 204
second = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/5')
assert second.status_code == 404
assert second.status_code != 204

tests.name: test_delete_squad_number_negative_returns_404
preconditions: Database minimum squad_number is 1; squad_number -1 does not exist
trace: R-PLAYER-015 — negative integer squad_number; well below any seeded value
BVA: catches mutations that might treat negative numbers as valid or return a different error code
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/-1')
assert response.status_code == 404
